failing.summary: The drive's line did not say what the drive is, how it starts agents or that it asks once.
The drive and signal lines read as seen on real runs; each now says its tests use stand-in agents.
The exit at the bound was given as one code; it is 0, or 3 where an issue was held back.
The page was stated without its two conditions: a chosen folder and a pull request a lane recorded armed.
A stop under an undecidable host session was left out; a stop is still set and only a lift or a folder choice is refused.
`facilitator.mode` was stated without `human` from any layer winning.
The headline implied every halted run names a pull request on its page.
The headline did not say that tests stand in the second account.
The guard line's list left out forms the registry refuses; it now says among others.
The guard line's prune wording was narrower than the rule.
The stop line had no caveat on the second account.
The listing was stated wider than what this account can read.
A stop was said to stay until lifted, with no word that an age cleaner may remove it from a temporary tree on Linux.
The stop line and the restart intent's line read oddly together.
`abcd agents` has no line of its own.
The drive ships under a planned intent, so its line can cite only the bound's issue.
The stop line names a run the stop had not halted and not new runs, and a halted run's refusal says the stop has lifted.

_reviewProvenance: Host-run docs-currency-reviewer over exact exports with a built binary: every line of the 0.16.2 CHANGELOG section and RELEASE.md, and the user-facing pages changed since v0.16.1. The first full pass found 2 major and 9 minor; the prose was recomposed by the changelog composer and the roll committed again. A second full pass returned PROMOTE with minors, three of which were applied in a third roll. A security review of the branch then found one more limit on a line, applied in a fourth roll. The same reviewer confirmed each of those lines and the digest against the code and returned PROMOTE on this commit.
provenanceExtra: The content commit is the fourth roll on this branch; each earlier roll was reverted by a new commit, with the third roll's receipts and captures reverted alongside it and then recorded again, and no history was rewritten.
